content:
maria: Hey team — FinServX asked for private deployment connectivity details for their POC. They want: 1) S2S VPN to our private control plane, 2) egress through their on‑prem proxy, and 3) static allowlist for health checks. Can eng confirm required IPs/ports and any gotchas?

dan: @maria quick Q — is their VPN terminating to a firewall that does SNAT? If they SNAT to a pool of public IPs we can use those for allowlist, otherwise we need per-session static IPs. Also: do they expect us to initiate connections, or only respond to their side?

maria: They said their edge does SNAT to a pair of static egress IPs (203.0.113.45/46). They will accept outbound 443 only, but want to know if any other ports needed (e.g., health checks, metrics). POC scheduled next Tue.

kevin: For Private deployments you typically only need 443 (TLS) to our private endpoint plus the control plane port for management (443 as well if mutual TLS). Healthchecks originate from our control plane IPs — we'll provide a small allowlist. Example firewall rule we usually share: 
```
# allow outbound to Redwood private endpoint
ALLOW TCP 203.0.113.45:443 -> 198.51.100.10:443  # example endpoint IP
# allow control-plane healthcheck IPs
ALLOW TCP 198.51.100.20:443
ALLOW TCP 198.51.100.21:443
```
Replace IPs with our real list.

maria: Copying the customer's note: "we will only permit egress to specific IPs, TLS only, and no inbound from internet. Appliance is behind a stateful firewall." They asked whether TCP keepalive/idle timeouts will break inference sessions.

alex: Idle timeouts can be an issue for long streaming sessions. Options: 1) use application-level heartbeats (we recommend keepalive pings every 30s), 2) use a proxy that supports longer TCP idle, or 3) route streaming through our Dedicated proxy (if available). For most POCs we configure small heartbeats. Also note: if they do TLS termination at the proxy (MITM), function-calling and request-level cert pinning may be affected.

pete: Security note: they asked about egress logging and key isolation. For Private we support customer KMS for model keys and audit logging forwarded to their SIEM. We should confirm whether the customer requires mutual TLS for the control channel or just client-cert validation. Also confirm accepted cipher suites (we default to TLS1.2+ with modern ciphers).

infra-bot: KB: Private deploy connectivity checklist -> https://docs.redwood.ai/private/connectivity (internal) :pushpin:

dan: Pricing question from the customer: if they route egress through their on‑prem proxy (BYO egress) do we charge outbound bandwidth? Sales needs an answer — does Private deployment include egress in the platform fee or is there a per-GB passthrough?

kevin: TL;DR: For Private (customer-hosted network) we don't bill for their on‑prem egress. If they use Redwood-managed outbound egress (we provide NAT or proxy) then there's an egress fee on top of the platform fee. I'll paste standard language for quotes — sales should confirm with finance for high-volume discounts.

maria: Perfect. Can eng provide the exact IP list and an official firewall snippet we can hand to the customer's network team? Also need a one‑pager for the POC runbook (ports, expected idle timeouts, sample tcpdump symptoms).

alex: I'll generate the allowlist and a 1-page runbook. Quick checklist: 
- Provide us with their NAT egress pair (they gave 203.0.113.45/46)
- Confirm whether VPN is BGP or static routes (BGP preferred for failover)
- If BGP, share ASN and prefixes to accept
- Confirm TLS inspection (yes/no)
- Agree heartbeat interval (we recommend 30s)

maria: They said VPN is static routes for the PoC but will consider BGP later. Putting a tech call on calendar for tomorrow 10am to finalize.

dan: For static-route VPNs note: if their firewall SNATs sessions differently per flow we need to ensure our healthchecks come from the same /32s consistently — I'll include a note in the runbook.

pete: I'll add security questionnaire answers for egress logging, KMS, and cipher suites. Also add SLA caveats if they choose BYO egress vs Redwood-managed egress.

kevin: Done — I'll upload the standard firewall snippet and pricing blurb to the shared drive after the tech call.

maria: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: — expecting final doc after the 10am call.
